claims.text: Eswatini vs USA: Dependency on Trade Taxes

claims.support: Global comparison of taxes on international trade (% of revenue)

claims.text: A global comparison showing how heavily different nations rely on international trade taxes for public revenue.
claims.support: Indicator measures taxes on international trade as a percentage of revenue across mapped countries and territories

claims.text: Eswatini gets 35.5% of government revenue from trade taxes. The USA gets 1.6%.
Eswatini is the world's highest, relying on border customs for over a third of its public funds.
The USA relies far less on border customs, taking in just 1.6% of its revenue there.
Side by side, Eswatini depends on trade taxes 22 times as much as the USA.
Across the globe, the median country collects 4.4% of total revenue from trade taxes.
claims.support: Median value of the 118 universe entries is around 4.4% (e.g., Rwanda 4.40%, Uzbekistan 4.40%)

claims.text: Bosnia is the world's lowest, drawing just 0.00001% of its revenue from border taxes.
How much does your country depend on international trade taxes?
